props.title: Les Misérables
props.initialSlug: Convict seeks redemption in epic musical revolution

sections.content: **Les Misérables (2012)** (2012) revolutionized movie musicals by recording vocals live on set, breaking from the lip-syncing tradition that defined films like **Chicago** (2002) and **Phantom of the Opera** (2004). Director Tom Hooper's intimate close-ups during songs like "I Dreamed a Dream" and "Empty Chairs at Empty Tables" created raw emotional intensity that previous stage-to-screen adaptations rarely achieved. Hugh Jackman's Jean Valjean and Anne Hathaway's Fantine set new standards for method acting in musicals, with Hathaway's devastating performance earning her an Oscar. Les Misérables|1998|Liam Neeson leads this non-musical adaptation that focuses on the cat-and-mouse chase between Valjean and Javert|Netflix The King's Speech|2010|Tom Hooper's Oscar-winning historical drama showcasing his talent for intimate character studies|HBO Max Chicago|2002|The glitzy, Oscar-winning adaptation that sparked the modern movie musical renaissance|Hulu

The film's revolutionary approach influenced later musicals like **Into the Woods** (2014) and **La La Land** (2016), which similarly prioritized actors' live performances over technical perfection. While some critics argued the close-up heavy direction diminished the story's epic scope, it undeniably brought Victor Hugo's themes of redemption, justice, and love into stark relief. The decision to cast established actors who could sing adequately rather than professional singers marked a significant shift from earlier musicals like **Evita** (1996).

The production design deserves special attention for creating a grimy, realistic 19th century Paris that contrasts sharply with the traditional stage versions. This gritty authenticity, combined with the live singing approach, helped ground the musical's more melodramatic elements. The massive barricade sequences and "One Day More" ensemble pieces prove Hooper could handle spectacle while maintaining emotional intimacy, though **The Greatest Showman** (2017) would later demonstrate an opposite approach of prioritizing polish over realism. Into the Woods|2014|Star-studded Sondheim adaptation balancing fairy tale whimsy with dark themes|Disney+ Evita|1996|Madonna stars in Alan Parker's ambitious adaptation of the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical|Prime Sweeney Todd|2007|Tim Burton's bloody take on Sondheim shows another way to adapt stage musicals|Netflix SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Movie Musicals

The success of **Les Misérables** (2012) emboldened studios to greenlight more ambitious musical projects. **In the Heights** (2021) adopted similar techniques for capturing live vocals while expanding the visual scope. Meanwhile, **West Side Story** (2021) combined classical Hollywood musical techniques with modern technological capabilities, showing how the genre continues evolving. Even rock musicals like **Rocketman** (2019) borrowed from Les Misérables' emotional authenticity while developing their own visual language.
